leads.title: Business Development Associate
leads.posting: About the job The short version: Who we're looking for: People who can influence. You're the kind of person who doesn't shy away from tough conversations - someone who listens deeply, understands what's holding a person back, and knows how to guide them to take action. If you've done Business Development, Inside Sales, B2C Sales, Admissions Counseling, or Consultative Sales, you'll find this role both challenging and meaningful. What this role is about: As part of the Admissions & Inside Sales team, you'll speak to students and professionals exploring Kraftshala's programs - understanding their goals, tackling their doubts, helping them evaluate program fit, and guiding them toward confident career decisions. Every lead you convert into an enrolment directly contributes to student outcomes and Kraftshala's growth. Why you should apply: Sales is one of the fastest ways to build skills that set apart great professionals. Here, you'll learn to communicate with impact, run structured consultative sales conversations, stay disciplined under pressure, and help people make decisions that genuinely change their careers. The learning curve is steep, the growth is fast, and the rewards - in both skills and incentives - are well worth the effort. About us: Kraftshala is India's largest skilling institution in terms of marketing & sales placements, with a 94% placement rate. We're building the world's most effective career launchpad across domains, backed by leaders from RedBus, NoBroker, Nestl , and Performics. The detailed version: As a Business Development Associate, you'll be the first point of contact for people exploring Kraftshala's programs. This is a 50% consultative admissions counseling + 50% structured inside sales role, where you guide applicants through clarity, empathy, and disciplined execution - while meeting your monthly enrolment, revenue, and pipeline conversion targets. Key Responsibilities: - Speak with students who show interest in our programs and guide

## Inspectable provenance

Not vibes. Not a score. Drop a file and read the manifest.

## The wrong question is “real or AI?”

The synthetic internet does not only create fake media. It creates **uncertainty around everything.**

RajISG starts where serious audiences already are: **provenance you can inspect** — not a vibes score.

*   Where did this come from?
*   Who first published it?
*   What changed before it reached me?

## With the coalition behind Content Authenticity

RajISG stands with the engineers, platforms, and institutions building **inspectable trust** — not vibes. The open spine is **Content Credentials** and **C2PA** so seals can travel across tools and borders.

## Seal content with Content Credentials

Attach a **cryptographic manifest** to what you publish: who signed, what changed, which disclosures apply. Viewers re-run the check — authenticity becomes a **habit**, not a brand promise alone.

## An ecosystem in synergy

Trusted creators, newsrooms, institutions, and everyday users — **same verification reflex** — pushing back on synthetic scams, misinformation, and silent swaps of “official-looking” media. **Authenticate the content.** Rescue the attention economy from pure spectacle.

## Protect your IP — seal every drop

We urge creators to **seal originals**, disclose edits with discipline, and carry a **verifiable link** in bios, press kits, and releases. Your work deserves a **credential trail** the internet can inspect.

## Integrity you can monetize

Sealing is how teams and creators **earn the click** — for sponsorships, official drops, portfolio proof, and the moments when only receipts matter.

Years of user testing, multiple iterations, and untangling the complexity of Mumbai's mixed network — suburban rail, metro, monorail, and everything in between — went into getting it right. Nine versions later, the V9 is an institutional-grade schematic covering every line in the network, available in four design styles. It's used by commuters, printed in offices, embedded in real estate brochures, and featured on the Mumbai Railway Police website. The map is free because the city deserves one that works.
